rawFindings.title: Incorrect image URL resolution in open_graph helper when path is relative
rawFindings.explanation: The new code forcibly prefixes the path with '/' and concatenates it to config.url, ignoring the current page URL. This breaks relative path resolution for images when the site is hosted in a subdirectory (e.g., 'http://example.com/blog'). The previous behavior used url.resolve(url || config.url, path), which correctly resolved relative paths based on the current page URL or site root. The change causes incorrect Open Graph image URLs leading to broken links.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original implementation using urlFn.resolve(url || config.url, path) to correctly handle both absolute and relative paths considering the page URL and site URL.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect image URL resolution for relative paths
rawFindings.explanation: The changed code replaces the use of 'urlFn.resolve(url || config.url, path)' with a manual concatenation 'config.url + path' after ensuring 'path' starts with '/'. This breaks the resolution of relative paths when the site is hosted in a subdirectory, causing incorrect 'og:image' URLs.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using 'urlFn.resolve(url || config.url, path)' for resolving image URLs to handle relative paths properly.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect absolute URL resolution for images
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces the use of url.resolve to compute the absolute URL for paths that are not full URLs. The old implementation resolved the image path relative to the page URL or site URL, correctly handling relative and absolute URLs including subdirectories. The new implementation forcibly prepends a '/' if missing and concatenates config.url + path, which breaks URLs when the site is hosted in a subdirectory, ignoring the page's URL path, causing incorrect image URLs.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original behavior using urlFn.resolve(url || config.url, path) to correctly resolve relative image paths based on current page URL or site URL, instead of concatenation.
